overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the executive session did not discuss the complainant's character, pre-meeting contacts did not reach a quorum, and excluding a member-complainant was discretionary.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to tell her it would discuss her character and reputation in its January 24, 2012 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Because there was no discussion of the complainant's reputation or character, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged secret pre-meeting discussions among members to agree on removing her from the deliberations.
allegations.key_passage: Because only one Committee member participated in this series of communications, there was no improper deliberation outside of an open meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the public was not told the need for executive session secrecy included discussing a member's character and requesting her recusal.
allegations.key_passage: Because there was no discussion of the complainant's reputation or character, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee deliberately excluded her from the full committee response to an Open Meeting Law complaint against it.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, whether or not she was permitted to participate in the executive session was a matter at the discretion of the Committee.
